title: this in Global Context
concept: In the global context, this refers to the global object (window/global)

steps.title: Global Variable Declaration
steps.explanation:
`var globalValue = 100` is declared at the global level.
A global variable declared with var becomes a **property of the global object (window)**.
steps.keyInsight: var globalValue = 100 is the same as window.globalValue = 100.

steps.title: Call getGlobalValue()
steps.explanation:
Call the `getGlobalValue()` function.
This is a regular function call, so this is the global object (window).
steps.keyInsight: In a regular function call, this = global object (window)

steps.title: Return this.globalValue
steps.explanation:
Inside the function, `this.globalValue` is returned.
Since this is window, window.globalValue = 100 is returned.

**Analogy**: It's like an employee (function) at a company (window) looking up 'this company's (this) asset (globalValue)'.
steps.analogy: It's like an employee (function) at a company (window) looking up 'this company's (this) asset (globalValue)'.

steps.title: Call strictGetValue()
steps.explanation:
Call the `strictGetValue()` function.
This function has `'use strict';` declared inside.
steps.keyInsight: In strict mode, this is undefined for regular function calls

steps.title: Return this in Strict Mode
steps.explanation:
Return `this` in strict mode.
In strict mode, this is **undefined** for a regular function call.
steps.keyInsight: Strict mode prevents accidentally modifying the global object.
steps.tip: ES6 modules and classes are in strict mode by default.

steps.title: Check for undefined
steps.explanation:
Check `result2 === undefined`.
Since the this returned from the strict mode function is undefined, `isUndefined = true`.
steps.keyInsight: How strict mode prevents global object pollution

steps.title: Print the Result
steps.explanation:
Execute `console.log(result1, isUndefined)`.
result1 is 100 and isUndefined is true.

quiz.explanation:
In strict mode, this is undefined for a regular function call.
This prevents accidentally modifying the global object.

misconceptions.wrong: this refers to the function itself
misconceptions.correct:
Absolutely not.
this is a property of the execution context determined by **how (and where) the function is called (the call site)**.
misconceptions.why:
this is determined at the time of function execution (not definition).
(Arrow functions are the exception.)

misconceptions.wrong: this inside a function is always the same value
misconceptions.correct:
No.
The same function can have a completely different this depending on whether it's called as `obj.method()` or just `method()`.
misconceptions.why: Who (which object) called the function determines what this is.

keyTakeaway: Global this = window, regular function this = window (strict mode: undefined)
